question: What are the three core things a basic computer does?

options.A: Storing drug dosages, calculating IV rates, and updating policies
options.B: Printing paper records, scanning IDs, and filing charts
options.C: Accepting data, processing it, and producing information
options.D: Connecting to the internet, sending emails, and blocking viruses

explanation: Think of a computer like a helpful assistant: it takes raw facts in, does some work on them, and gives you useful results for patient care!

question: What is the benefit of comparing unit prices while shopping?

options.A: It determines how long the food item will last in the refrigerator
options.B: It helps the cashier calculate the total sales tax accurately
options.C: It reveals the true cost of an item per standard weight or volume
options.D: It shows which brand contains the highest amount of artificial preservatives

explanation: Brilliant! Unit pricing cuts through sneaky package sizes to show you which product actually gives you more value for your money.

question: Which condition happens when the body makes insulin, but the cells do not respond to it properly (insulin resistance)?

options.A: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
options.B: Primary lactic acidosis
options.C: Phenylketonuria
options.D: Type 1 diabetes mellitus

explanation: In Type 2 diabetes, the pancreas still produces insulin, but the body's cells have become resistant to it, locking glucose out and leaving it stuck in the blood.

question: Which body sets the legal scope of practice for Nigerian midwives?

options.A: Pharmacists Council of Nigeria
options.B: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria
options.C: West African Health Organization
options.D: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: Great memory! The NMCN is our guiding regulatory body that oversees nursing and midwifery training and practice in Nigeria.

question: How do you know for sure if a patient truly understood your health education instructions?

options.A: Asking the patient to explain the instructions back in their own words
options.B: Ensuring the nurse spoke clearly without using medical jargon
options.C: Writing down all the medication dosages on a whiteboard
options.D: Handing the patient a printed pamphlet before leaving the room

explanation: This is the classic 'teach-back' method! Asking them to explain it in their own words helps you catch any confusion without making them feel small.

question: In the ABCDE guide for checking moles, what does the letter 'D' stand for?

options.A: Density
options.B: Depth
options.C: Diameter
options.D: Dryness

explanation: You got it! 'D' is for Diameter—moles that are growing larger than 6 millimeters need a doctor's attention.

question: Through which part of the spinal cord do incoming sensory nerve signals enter?

options.A: Dorsal root
options.B: Lateral horn
options.C: Central canal
options.D: Ventral root

explanation: Sensory information always comes in through the back door—the dorsal root—bringing messages from the rest of the body into the central nervous system.

question: What is the main cause of Maternal Depletion Syndrome?

options.A: Repeated, closely spaced pregnancies without adequate recovery time
options.B: A sudden genetic mutation triggered by multiple childbirths
options.C: Exposure to harsh environmental toxins during early adulthood
options.D: Consuming a diet high in processed foods during lactation

explanation: Maternal depletion happens when a mother's body doesn't get enough breathing room to heal and rebuild its nutrient stores between pregnancies.

question: What is the main goal of having a menu in a hospital or clinic kitchen?

options.A: To list food and drink items to meet nutritional and financial needs
options.B: To calculate the daily profit margin of the hospital kitchen
options.C: To dictate the cleaning schedule for the food preparation staff
options.D: To provide a strict legal record of patient drug administration

explanation: A menu is simply a guide to make sure meals meet nutritional, cultural, and budget needs!

question: What crucial warning must you give a patient who takes daily anti-seizure medication?

options.A: Only take the pills on days when you feel a headache coming on
options.B: Never stop taking the medication suddenly without consulting your doctor
options.C: Stop the medication immediately if you go one week without a seizure
options.D: Take a double dose whenever you feel stressed or tired

explanation: Spot on! Quitting anti-seizure meds abruptly can trigger dangerous rebound seizures or status epilepticus. Always taper safely with a doctor's guidance.

question: A Nigerian nurse notices a high rate of infant malnutrition in her village. What is the BEST application of primary health care principles to solve this?

options.A: Punish parents who fail to bring their children for monthly weight checks
options.B: Wait for international donors to ship expensive tinned baby formula to the clinic
options.C: Refer every malnourished baby to the national teaching hospital in the city
options.D: Organize a community workshop using local foods to teach mothers balanced meal preparation

explanation: Using local food resources and educating mothers empowers the community with sustainable, appropriate solutions. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h8)

question: A patient with severe internal bleeding from a car crash is most likely to develop which type of shock?

options.A: Neurogenic shock
options.B: Hypovolemic shock
options.C: Anaphylactic shock
options.D: Cardiogenic shock

explanation: Hypovolemic shock is caused by a drastic loss of blood volume circulating in the body. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h5)

question: Where does home quarantine take place?

options.A: At the airport arrival lounge
options.B: Inside a specialized infectious disease hospital ward
options.C: In a government-run military camp
options.D: At the individual's private residence

explanation: Home quarantine allows exposed persons to remain in their own homes while restricting outside visitors and public outings. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h3)

question: Long-term hookworm infection most commonly leads to which major health problem?

options.A: Chronic kidney failure
options.B: Elevated blood pressure
options.C: Obstructive jaundice
options.D: Iron-deficiency anemia

explanation: Hookworms hook onto the intestinal wall and feed on blood, which over time causes significant blood loss and leads to iron-deficiency anemia.

question: What is a main difference between personal and organisational objectives?

options.A: Personal goals focus on individual growth, while organisational goals focus on collective institutional success
options.B: Personal goals never involve learning or professional development
options.C: Personal goals are always written by the government, while organisational goals are written by nurses
options.D: Organisational goals only care about individual staff salaries

explanation: Think of it simply: personal goals are about your own growth and pocket, while organisational goals are about the success and health standards of the whole hospital.

question: When does an infection officially count as a healthcare-associated infection?

options.A: Before the patient ever enters the clinic
options.B: Immediately following any minor injection
options.C: At least 48 hours after hospital admission
options.D: Within the first two hours of arrival

explanation: The 48-hour window helps differentiate infections the patient brought in with them from those caught while inside the facility. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h1)

question: A mother wants to mark her newborn baby for protection. How should the nurse best handle this counseling?

options.A: Threaten to call security if she attempts the procedure
options.B: Perform the cuts safely using hospital surgical blades
options.C: Explain infection risks gently and suggest safer alternatives
options.D: Ignore the conversation because it is a private family matter

explanation: That's brilliant nursing! Respectful education bridges cultural beliefs with health safety without pushing the client away.

question: Which nursing check is most important when evaluating a patient's risk for vaccine-preventable diseases?

options.A: Testing the patient's blood pressure in both arms
options.B: Reviewing the patient's personal immunization records
options.C: Checking the patient's skin elasticity for signs of dehydration
options.D: Measuring the patient's daily fluid intake and output

explanation: Well done! Looking at immunization cards gives you the exact history you need to know which diseases they are protected against.

question: Why is it important to encourage a labouring mum to empty her bladder regularly?

options.A: To speed up cervical dilation past 10 centimeters
options.B: To stop Braxton Hicks contractions from returning
options.C: To prevent the bladder from obstructing fetal descent
options.D: To collect urine for a daily routine glucose test

explanation: Brilliant! A full bladder gets in the way like a water balloon in the pelvis, which can slow down the baby's journey down the birth canal.

question: Why is sterilization stricter and more powerful than standard disinfection?

options.A: It only applies to items that touch intact human skin
options.B: It can be completed in a few seconds using simple wipes
options.C: It targets and kills bacterial spores as well as vegetative cells
options.D: It is performed using mild soaps and warm running water

explanation: Disinfection kills a lot of germs, but tough bacterial spores can survive it. Sterilization goes the extra mile to destroy those resilient spores completely!

question: What does an Incremental Cost-Effectiveness Ratio (ICER) tell a nurse administrator?

options.A: The exact percentage of patients who will refuse medication
options.B: The total yearly budget needed to run the emergency department
options.C: The extra cost required to gain one additional unit of health outcome
options.D: The net profit generated by surgical procedures over a quarter

explanation: ICER simply asks: 'Is paying extra for this new treatment worth the extra health benefit we get?' It measures that trade-off.

question: Which of the following is a direct obstetric complication linked to female genital mutilation?

options.A: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.B: Obstructed labor and tearing
options.C: Pregnancy-induced hypertension
options.D: Hyperemesis gravidarum severity

explanation: Scar tissue from these practices restricts the birth canal, leading to difficult deliveries and severe tearing. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T18#GNS312_U1_T18_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of performing a skin biopsy in dermatology?

options.A: To obtain tissue samples for definitive microscopic diagnosis
options.B: To instantly kill bacteria inside a deep skin abscess
options.C: To remove unwanted benign moles for cosmetic reasons
options.D: To rehydrate severely dry and cracking skin layers

explanation: A biopsy removes a small piece of skin tissue so a pathologist can examine it under a microscope to confirm diseases like skin cancer or severe inflammation. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T10#GNS213_U5_T10_h2)

question: What do we call the map-like representation of the body's muscles laid out across the motor cortex?

options.A: Brodmann blueprint
options.B: Pyramidal map
options.C: Sensory dermatome
options.D: Motor homunculus

explanation: Spot on! The 'motor homunculus' is the quirky little brain map showing how cortical space is shared out among body parts.

question: Your instructor wants to grade how well you show empathy and active listening during a patient chat. Which tool is best suited for this?

options.A: A binary checklist of yes or no procedural steps
options.B: A rating scale with descriptive performance levels
options.C: A multiple-choice pharmacology quiz
options.D: A timed medication calculation test

explanation: Communication has shades of quality, so a rating scale works much better than a simple yes/no checkbox to capture how well you connect with patients.

question: As a nurse, what is your primary role during an emergency intracardiac injection?

options.A: Performing the needle insertion into the chest wall
options.B: Preparing equipment and monitoring the cardiac rhythm
options.C: Prescribing the correct dosage of emergency drugs
options.D: Documenting the discharge summary for the patient

explanation: Teamwork is key in emergencies! You support the doctor by getting gear ready, timing events, and watching the monitor to see how the patient reacts.

question: Why do seasonal rains often cause a drop in immunization coverage in rural areas?

options.A: Dirt roads and broken bridges make travel to health centers difficult
options.B: Rain causes widespread power outages that destroy all vaccine vials
options.C: Mothers are legally forbidden from taking children outside during storms
options.D: Vaccines wash away easily when exposed to heavy rainwater

explanation: Correct! Flooded paths and bad roads physically isolate villages from health centers during the rainy season.

question: Why does the physical form of a medication matter so much to a nurse?

options.A: It decides the exact colour the patient will see
options.B: It dictates the correct and safe route of administration
options.C: It guarantees that side effects will never occur
options.D: It proves whether the drug is synthetic or plant-based

explanation: The physical form of a drug determines how it must safely enter the body, such as by mouth, injection, or skin application. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T7#GNS125_U2_T7_h1)

question: Which of these is a NORMAL finding and NOT a danger sign for a new mother?

options.A: Soaking through two large sanitary pads in one hour
options.B: A high fever with chills
options.C: Mild tiredness after caring for the baby at night
options.D: Sudden severe chest pain and trouble breathing

explanation: Every new mum is tired! But heavy bleeding, chest pain, and high fever are urgent warning signs that need immediate attention.

question: What is the most popular theory explaining how endometriosis starts in the first place?

options.A: Congenital uterine absence
options.B: Retrograde menstruation
options.C: Lymphatic vessel blockage
options.D: Primary ovarian failure

explanation: Retrograde menstruation is like a traffic mix-up where menstrual blood flows backward through the fallopian tubes and into the pelvis instead of leaving the body.

question: Why do nurses need to track daily medication use closely in a field clinic?

options.A: To calculate daily hospital profits for insurance
options.B: To keep pharmacy staff busy with paperwork
options.C: To predict shortages and reorder supplies before running out
options.D: To prove to patients that drugs are expensive

explanation: Smart nursing! Keeping an eye on daily counts helps you spot when you're running low so you can reorder life-saving items ahead of time.

question: At 28 weeks, an ultrasound shows a slight thickening of the mother's left heart ventricle. What does this mean?

options.A: It is a normal physiological response to increased cardiac workload
options.B: It indicates long-standing chronic hypertension
options.C: It points to an acute myocardial infarction
options.D: It shows early signs of congenital heart failure

explanation: Exactly! The heart muscle works harder during pregnancy, so it thickens just a little bit to handle the extra load safely.

question: Which action best shows you are advocating for your patient at the end of life?

options.A: Withholding pain medication to keep the patient awake for visiting relatives
options.B: Ignoring advance directives if the attending physician disagrees with them
options.C: Ensuring a documented DNR order is followed despite objections from distant relatives
options.D: Following the loudest family member's demand to start aggressive CPR

explanation: As a nurse, your duty is to protect the patient's documented wishes, even when family members disagree.

question: What is a 'Call to Action' (CTA) in an advocacy message?

options.A: A legal warning issued to government officials who delay funds
options.B: A list of symptoms used to diagnose infectious diseases
options.C: A medical emergency number to call during a disease outbreak
options.D: A clear instruction telling the audience exactly what to do next

explanation: You've got this! A CTA simply tells your listeners what practical step they can take right away to help.

question: How does a community health nurse use epidemiological thinking during a clinic shift?

options.A: By focusing strictly on the medical chart of the person in front of them
options.B: By ordering expensive scans for every patient with a headache
options.C: By looking for patterns and causes of illness in the local community
options.D: By diagnosing complex genetic disorders without lab tests

explanation: Exactly! Community health nurses connect the dots between individual illnesses and broader local trends to help everyone stay healthy. Great thinking!

question: As a nurse, what is your main goal when doing a risk assessment during antenatal care?

options.A: To accurately predict the exact day and hour of delivery
options.B: To eliminate the need for any laboratory blood tests
options.C: To detect potential complications early before they become life-threatening
options.D: To diagnose all genetic disorders in the unborn infant

explanation: Brilliant! Screening lets us spot moms who need extra support or specialized care early on, keeping both mother and baby safe.

question: What does it mean when a child's plotted dots form a line pointing upward, running parallel to the reference curves?

options.A: Normal, healthy physical growth
options.B: Immediate risk of severe acute malnutrition
options.C: An error in the initial birth weight record
options.D: Chronic stunting due to repeated infections

explanation: When the curve follows the expected upward path, it's a great sign that the child is gaining weight and growing steadily!

question: How can a nurse best handle personal biases when caring for a stigmatized patient?

options.A: Reading legal textbooks to punish patients who break social norms
options.B: Asking another nurse to handle all female reproductive health cases
options.C: Practicing active self-reflection and discussing feelings with supportive peers
options.D: Suppressing all emotions until the end of the calendar year

explanation: Talking things through with supportive colleagues and checking your own mindset helps you catch hidden biases before they affect your patient care.

question: Why do family members often feel so distressed when a dying patient stops eating?

options.A: They are worried about the cost of purchasing groceries
options.B: They know that eating is the only cure for their illness
options.C: They believe the hospital kitchen is refusing to cook
options.D: They may view food as a symbol of care and worry the patient is being neglected

explanation: Very true. In our cultures, feeding someone is a deep act of love, so seeing them refuse food can feel heartbreaking to the family.

question: Which type of bedpan is best to use for a patient who has a broken hip?

options.A: A standard high-backed bedpan
options.B: A rigid plastic commode chair
options.C: A fracture pan
options.D: A pediatric incontinence ring

explanation: Fracture pans are shallow, meaning you don't have to lift the patient's hips high up. This is a lifesaver for avoiding extra pain or injury when dealing with hip or pelvic bones!

question: Why do we prefer asking open-ended questions when interviewing a patient for contact tracing?

options.A: They help jog the patient's memory and uncover forgotten activities
options.B: They prevent the patient from asking questions about their illness
options.C: They legally bind the patient to follow quarantine instructions
options.D: They shorten the interview time so the nurse can leave early

explanation: Yes! Instead of a simple 'yes' or 'no', open questions let patients talk freely so they can remember places and people they might otherwise forget.

question: A patient receiving a strong chemotherapy drug through a peripheral IV suddenly complains of a burning pain, and the area starts swelling up. What is your very first action?

options.A: Stop the infusion immediately and disconnect the tubing.
options.B: Flush the IV line rapidly with normal saline to clear the drug.
options.C: Massage the arm firmly to help the drug spread out faster.
options.D: Apply a cold ice pack directly over the swollen area.

explanation: Safety first! Stopping the infusion right away prevents any more harsh fluid from leaking into the tissue and causing damage.

question: What tragic emotional outcome is sometimes seen among young brides who feel completely trapped with no way out?

options.A: Bipolar manic episodes
options.B: Suicide and self-harm
options.C: Dissociative identity disorder
options.D: Pathological compulsive gambling

explanation: That's correct. Overwhelming hopelessness and a lack of support drive some desperate young brides to self-harm or suicide.

question: A client expresses fear that an injectable contraceptive will cause permanent infertility. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Agree that hormonal drugs permanently damage the womb and suggest avoiding them
options.B: Insist she takes the injection anyway because healthcare workers know best
options.C: Explain that fertility generally returns after the drug wears off, though it may take a few months
options.D: Tell the client that her fears are unfounded and scold her for listening to myths

explanation: Nurses must address client fears respectfully with accurate medical facts rather than dismissing or forcing them. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h3)

question: Why should nurses never use ordinary kitchen spoons to measure out liquid medicines?

options.A: Liquid medications will stain metal spoons permanently
options.B: Hospital policy strictly forbids touching any utensil from a kitchen
options.C: Plastic spoons react chemically with syrup and destroy the drug
options.D: Household spoons vary widely in size and do not provide accurate doses

explanation: Spot on! Kitchen spoons come in all shapes and sizes, which can easily lead to giving too much or too little medicine.

question: Why should nurses avoid forcing disaster survivors to immediately talk about the graphic details of their trauma?

options.A: Survivors lose their legal right to medical treatment if they speak about the event
options.B: Hospital administrative policy strictly forbids nurses from listening to stories
options.C: Talking about trauma instantly causes permanent physical paralysis in adults
options.D: It can re-traumatize the individual and worsen acute psychological distress

explanation: Pushing someone to relive a horrific event before they are ready can overwhelm their mind and make their emotional shock even worse.

question: Why should you avoid using your thumb when checking a patient's radial pulse?

options.A: Using the thumb violates standard hospital infection control rules
options.B: The thumb has its own distinct pulse that can confuse the count
options.C: The thumb applies too much pressure and collapses the artery
options.D: The thumb is too insensitive to feel the soft arterial wall

explanation: Your thumb has its own strong pulse! If you use it, you might end up counting your own heartbeat instead of the patient's. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h3)

question: What is the primary function of lymph nodes?

options.A: Filtering lymph and trapping foreign invaders
options.B: Producing new red blood cells
options.C: Pumping lymph fluid through the body
options.D: Storing excess dietary fats

explanation: Lymph nodes act as filters that catch bacteria, viruses, and debris before fluid returns to the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h3)

question: What is a great way for a father to support the mother after childbirth?

options.A: Isolating the newborn from all family members
options.B: Taking over exclusive breastfeeding duties from the mother
options.C: Assisting with household chores to help the mother rest
options.D: Refusing to allow visitors into the family compound

explanation: New mothers need plenty of physical rest to recover, so a partner stepping in with chores is a huge help!

question: Where do traditional medicines mostly come from?

options.A: Plants, animals, and minerals
options.B: Roots, leaves, and bark
options.C: Fungi, bacteria, and insects
options.D: Synthetics, herbs, and vitamins

explanation: You'll find that traditional healing systems rely heavily on what is freely available around them—using gifts from the plant kingdom, animal parts, and natural minerals. Great job thinking about your roots!

question: Which body tissue is mainly responsible for movement and pumping blood?

options.A: Nervous tissue
options.B: Muscle tissue
options.C: Connective tissue
options.D: Epithelial tissue

explanation: Muscle tissue is built to contract and shorten, making it the powerhouse behind every movement you make.

question: Why should you leave tubes and lines in place and document them if an autopsy is expected?

options.A: To make it easier for the mortuary worker to remove them
options.B: To prove the nurse attempted emergency resuscitation
options.C: To ensure the hospital can bill the family for the supplies
options.D: To prevent tampering with evidence or forensic findings

explanation: Spot on! Leaving them alone and documenting them keeps forensic evidence intact for investigators.

question: Which sign tells a nurse that a local skin infection is starting to spread through the whole body?

options.A: Elevated body temperature and abnormal white blood cell counts
options.B: A decrease in the patient's daily fluid intake and urine output
options.C: Changes in the patient's preference for sweet or salty foods
options.D: The patient's ability to walk unassisted down the hospital hallway

explanation: Fever (elevated temperature) and high white blood cell counts are classic systemic red flags telling you the infection is going body-wide.

question: Which level of the Nigerian healthcare system does community health nursing support the most?

options.A: Primary health care
options.B: International health agencies
options.C: Private specialist care
options.D: Tertiary healthcare

explanation: You nailed it! Community health nurses work right at the grassroots level, which is the solid foundation of primary health care in Nigeria.

question: What is the medical term for the gradual loss of muscle mass and strength as people age?

options.A: Presbyopia
options.B: Sarcopenia
options.C: Osteoporosis
options.D: Atherosclerosis

explanation: Spot on! Sarcopenia is the natural, progressive shrinking of skeletal muscle that happens as we grow older.

question: Which type of thread is used for outer skin stitches and needs to be taken out after a few days?

options.A: Absorbable suture
options.B: Non-absorbable suture
options.C: Catgut suture
options.D: Biodegradable thread

explanation: Non-absorbable materials like nylon give strong outer support while the skin heals, and we remove them during a follow-up visit. Easypz!

question: Which of the following is an example of a hierarchical communication barrier?

options.A: A junior nurse being too intimidated to report a abnormal sign to a senior doctor
options.B: A nurse misunderstanding a medical term written in a foreign language
options.C: A noisy infusion pump beeping loudly in a crowded intensive care unit
options.D: A tired staff member forgetting to read the morning shift handover notes

explanation: Fear of authority and strict power gaps create hierarchical barriers that prevent vital patient safety information from traveling upward. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h4)

question: What is the correct way to apply prophylactic eye ointment in a newborn?

options.A: Flood the entire closed eyelid with liquid solution
options.B: Massage the upper eyelid vigorously after application
options.C: Apply into the lower conjunctival sac without touching the eye
options.D: Place the ointment directly onto the center of the cornea

explanation: Spot on! Putting it in the lower sac keeps the tube clean and protects the baby's eye from accidental injury. You're thinking like a real nurse!

question: What is a major safety worry for a patient dealing with dysphagia (difficulty swallowing) after brain surgery?

options.A: Loss of arm movement
options.B: Permanent hearing loss
options.C: Aspiration pneumonia
options.D: Sudden high blood pressure

explanation: You nailed it! When swallowing is weak, food or saliva can slip down the windpipe into the lungs. This puts the patient at high risk for a dangerous lung infection called aspiration pneumonia.

question: What is the main difference between a direct and an indirect obstetric death?

options.A: Direct deaths occur during labor, while indirect deaths occur in the postpartum period
options.B: Direct deaths are caused by infections, while indirect deaths are caused by bleeding
options.C: Direct deaths happen in the hospital, while indirect deaths happen at home
options.D: Direct deaths are from pregnancy complications, while indirect deaths are from pre-existing diseases worsened by pregnancy

explanation: Spot on! Direct causes come straight from pregnancy or childbirth issues (like bleeding), while indirect causes happen when a pre-existing condition (like heart disease or malaria) gets worse because of the pregnancy.

question: How do you place AED pads on a patient who has a pacemaker lump on their upper left chest?

options.A: Place the AED pad at least one inch away from the device
options.B: Refuse to use the AED because implanted devices block shocks entirely
options.C: Disable the pacemaker using a magnet before applying the pads
options.D: Place the AED pad directly over the bulge to improve shock delivery

explanation: Just place the pad about an inch away from the pacemaker bulge. If you put it right on top, it can absorb the shock energy and damage the implanted device.

question: As a nurse, what is a crucial check to make *before* a patient goes for a liver biopsy?

options.A: Check that clotting blood tests are safe and consent is signed
options.B: Perform a minor surgery to drain belly fluid
options.C: Give them strong general anesthesia right in the ward
options.D: Make sure they eat a large heavy meal

explanation: Spot on! Safety first—always verify clotting labs and make sure the patient understands and signs the consent form before the procedure.

question: A community health nurse organizes a routine childhood vaccination drive at a local clinic. What level of prevention is this?

options.A: Secondary prevention
options.B: Tertiary prevention
options.C: Primordial prevention
options.D: Primary prevention

explanation: You got it! Giving immunizations protects healthy people from getting sick in the first place, which is primary prevention.

question: What happens if the immune system gets confused and fails to recognize the body's own tissues?

options.A: Blood pressure drops to dangerously low levels
options.B: An autoimmune disorder develops
options.C: Red blood cells stop carrying oxygen
options.D: The body becomes completely immune to all viruses

explanation: You've got it! When the immune system stops recognizing 'self,' it mistakenly attacks healthy tissues, leading to autoimmune conditions.

question: What is the primary goal of home health care?

options.A: To replace traditional long-term nursing home facilities
options.B: To provide permanent 24-hour bedside critical care
options.C: To help patients recover and live independently at home
options.D: To reduce the workload of busy hospital physicians

explanation: Home health services focus on bringing medical and support care to the residence so individuals can manage conditions and recover safely where they live. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why do we treat active tuberculosis with multiple drugs instead of just one antibiotic?

options.A: It makes the treatment course last much longer.
options.B: It eliminates the need for any nutritional support.
options.C: It lowers the risk of common stomach upsets.
options.D: It prevents the bacteria from easily developing drug resistance.

explanation: Hitting the TB bacteria with a combination of strong drugs makes it nearly impossible for the germs to mutate and outsmart the treatment.

question: A community nurse helps a stroke patient practice daily walking exercises to regain strength. Which component of comprehensive care does this represent?

options.A: Disease prevention
options.B: Rehabilitative care
options.C: Health promotion
options.D: Curative services

explanation: Helping a patient recover lost functions and achieve independence after an illness or injury falls directly under rehabilitative care. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h3)

question: A metal welder asks you for advice on how to protect their eyes while working. What is the best primary prevention advice?

options.A: Wash the eyes thoroughly with clean water at the end of each shift.
options.B: Take high-dose vitamin supplements every morning before starting work.
options.C: Wear certified protective face shields and safety goggles consistently.
options.D: Rest the eyes in complete darkness for ten minutes every hour.

explanation: Physical barriers are key here! Certified face shields and safety goggles block flying sparks and dangerous welding light rays right at the source, keeping those eyes safe.

question: A patient with viral meningitis asks if they need strong antibiotics. What should you tell them?

options.A: Antibiotics are not prescribed because viral infections do not respond to antibacterial drugs.
options.B: Antibiotics will cure the virus if taken within the first twenty-four hours.
options.C: You need high doses of penicillin immediately to prevent hearing loss.
options.D: Only herbal medications can help clear up viral infections in the brain.

explanation: Remember: antibiotics only kill bacteria, not viruses! For viral meningitis, we focus on supportive care to keep the patient comfortable while their body fights it off.

question: A couple struggling to conceive asks for a simple change they can make first. What is the best initial nursing advice?

options.A: Begin in-vitro fertilization immediately
options.B: Undergo exploratory pelvic surgery
options.C: Stop smoking and limit alcohol intake together
options.D: Take high-dose testosterone supplements

explanation: Cleaning up daily habits like quitting smoking is a safe, effective first step before jumping into medical procedures.

question: What are the classic signs of a fungal nail infection (onychomycosis)?

options.A: Soft, concave, spoon-shaped surfaces
options.B: Complete absence of the nail plate
options.C: Bright blue and swollen nail beds
options.D: Thick, yellow, and brittle nail plates

explanation: Well done! Fungal infections usually make the nail look discolored (yellow or brown), very thick, and easy to crumble.

question: Why do we say food is like medicine when it comes to preventing long-term illnesses?

options.A: Eating specific foods replaces the need for surgical interventions entirely
options.B: Food items can be prescribed by nurses just like pharmaceutical drugs
options.C: Nutrients cure all infectious pathogens without the need for antibiotics
options.D: Dietary choices directly influence the development of conditions like diabetes and hypertension

explanation: You got it! Eating healthy meals helps keep lifestyle diseases like high blood pressure and diabetes away, acting just like preventive medicine.

question: How is a patient usually positioned immediately after a lumbar puncture?

options.A: Flat in bed
options.B: Trendelenburg position
options.C: High Fowler's position
options.D: Standing up and walking

explanation: Spot on! Lying flat helps the tiny puncture hole seal up and lowers the chance of a stubborn spinal headache.

question: Why is using a gait belt so helpful when assisting a patient to stand and walk?

options.A: It corrects the patient's posture automatically without active effort
options.B: It gives the nurse a secure grip to prevent falls if the patient loses balance
options.C: It completely stops the patient from feeling dizzy while standing up
options.D: It replaces the need for a physical therapist during early walking sessions

explanation: A gait belt gives you a safe handle around the patient's waist, making it much easier to catch them safely if their legs wobble.

question: As student nurses, we always hear about confidentiality. What does it actually mean?

options.A: Documenting all personal feelings in public charts
options.B: Keeping patient information private and secure
options.C: Sharing patient stories with the entire clinic staff
options.D: Telling family members everything the patient says

explanation: Confidentiality means what happens in the counselling session stays between you and the patient. Trust is everything!

question: Why do hospitals require standard precautions for every single patient, no matter their diagnosis?

options.A: Infectious diseases only spread after a laboratory confirms them
options.B: It saves time so nurses do not have to check patient charts
options.C: Patients prefer knowing their care involves extra safety steps
options.D: Any patient's blood or body fluid can carry hidden infectious pathogens

explanation: You can't always tell who has an infection by looking at them. Treating every body fluid as potentially infectious keeps you safe every time.

question: What is the term for emotional exhaustion and numbness that nurses feel after dealing with too much trauma?

options.A: Compassion fatigue
options.B: Post-surgical shock
options.C: Florence Nightingale syndrome
options.D: Professional burnout syndrome

explanation: Compassion fatigue happens when seeing heavy, stressful cases day after day drains your emotional tank. It is totally normal to feel this way, which is why self-care matters!

question: What is considered the gold-standard, first-choice treatment for chronic insomnia?

options.A: High-dose benzodiazepines every night
options.B: Complete sensory deprivation therapy
options.C: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I)
options.D: Over-the-counter antihistamines

explanation: CBT-I is the top recommendation! It helps retrain your brain and sleep habits for long-term success without any risk of drug dependence.

question: Why do we need a special pressurized flush system for an arterial monitoring line?

options.A: Arterial pressure is high enough to push blood backward into the tubing
options.B: It cools the blood down before it reaches the electronic monitor
options.C: It speeds up the rate of intravenous fluid replacement for dehydration
options.D: It eliminates the need to ever flush the catheter with heparin

explanation: Because arterial pressure is so strong, it will easily push blood right back up into your IV tubing and cause a clot if you don't use steady, pressurized pressure to keep it clear!

question: What is a very common cause of false alarms on a portable pulse oximeter while moving a patient?

options.A: Normal room lighting brightness
options.B: Fresh battery installation
options.C: High room humidity levels
options.D: Motion artifact and shivering

explanation: Movement or shivering shakes the sensor around (motion artifact), confusing the machine and leading to wild or false readings.

question: What is the main reason healthcare providers use drug classification systems?

options.A: To completely eliminate the need for doctor prescriptions
options.B: To help nurses administer medications safely and anticipate effects
options.C: To ensure all medications cost the same amount of money
options.D: To make drug manufacturing companies produce fewer pills

explanation: Grouping drugs helps nurses predict how a medication will work and watch out for specific side effects during patient care. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h1)

question: What is the main job of the rods in our retina?

options.A: Regulating the amount of light entering the pupil
options.B: Producing fluid for the front of the eye
options.C: Enabling sharp color vision in bright light
options.D: Functioning in dim light and detecting motion

explanation: Think of rods as your night-vision helpers! They are super sensitive to low light and movement, which helps you get around in the dark.

question: Why do drugs with a narrow therapeutic index need very careful blood monitoring?

options.A: The safe dose is very close to the toxic dose.
options.B: They can only be given through intravenous infusion.
options.C: They stop working after three days of administration.
options.D: The patient builds resistance to them very quickly.

explanation: With a narrow therapeutic index, the line between 'helping' and 'harming' is very thin. Careful monitoring keeps our patients safe!

question: How should a nurse best approach a caregiver who expresses fear and hesitation about routine childhood vaccines?

options.A: Scold the parent for ignoring professional medical advice
options.B: Report the parent to local law enforcement authorities
options.C: Listen respectfully and provide clear, reassuring education
options.D: Ignore their concerns and administer the vaccines anyway

explanation: Building trust through empathetic listening and clear, respectful communication is the most effective way to address vaccine hesitancy and correct rumors. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h8)

question: A nurse wants to teach mothers how to prevent severe dehydration from watery stools in infants. What should be the main demonstration?

options.A: How to mix and give oral rehydration salt solution
options.B: How to isolate the child in a dark room
options.C: How to completely stop the baby from drinking fluids
options.D: How to perform emergency intravenous surgery

explanation: Teaching mothers home preparation of oral rehydration solution saves lives by treating early fluid loss before it becomes critical. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h2)

question: Why don't we use the intraarterial route for everyday medications like regular IVs?

options.A: Intravenous medications are always cheaper to manufacture
options.B: Arteries have no blood flow once a needle enters them
options.C: High arterial pressure makes access and maintenance complex and risky
options.D: Drugs given this way are instantly destroyed by liver enzymes

explanation: Arteries pump blood at a much higher pressure than veins! This makes them tricky to manage and prone to serious bleeding, so we save them for special situations.

question: A nurse quietly accepts extra shifts without complaint while feeling deeply resentful and exhausted. Which style is this nurse showing?

options.A: Aggressive
options.B: Passive-aggressive
options.C: Passive
options.D: Assertive

explanation: Constantly giving in without voicing your limits is a classic sign of passive behavior. [learn more](GST321_U7_T5#GST321_U7_T5_h2)

question: Why is the real-world failure rate for natural methods usually higher than the textbook 'perfect use' rate?

options.A: Manufacturing defects occur in calendar charts
options.B: Human error and inconsistent tracking happen in daily life
options.C: Body temperature sensors expire after one month
options.D: Government policies restrict natural birth control methods

explanation: A method might look foolproof on paper, but real life gets busy! Missing a day of charting or miscalculating a window easily leads to human error.

question: A community nurse in a rural village talks with local elders before starting a malaria prevention drive. What is the nurse showing here?

options.A: Enforcement of strict punitive laws
options.B: Exclusive reliance on foreign aid
options.C: Collaboration and cultural respect
options.D: Medical paternalism and isolation

explanation: Brilliant! Involving local leaders builds trust and ensures the health program will actually work and last.

question: Why are home-based antenatal visits especially helpful for women living in rural areas?

options.A: It completely removes the risk of any pregnancy complication
options.B: It ensures the mother delivers at home every single time
options.C: It overcomes the barrier of long-distance travel to health facilities
options.D: It lowers the cost of buying hospital equipment

explanation: Distance is a huge challenge for many rural mothers. Bringing care to them keeps them regular with their check-ups!

question: How does eating too much sugar over a long time lead to insulin resistance?

options.A: Sugar molecules coat the pancreas and permanently stop it from making any digestive enzymes
options.B: Constant high blood sugar forces the pancreas to oversecrete insulin until body cells stop responding
options.C: High sugar levels destroy every insulin receptor in the liver instantly
options.D: The kidneys block all insulin from entering the bloodstream to protect the heart

explanation: Imagine constantly shouting at someone—eventually, they stop listening! High glucose levels force your pancreas to pump out so much insulin that your body cells eventually tune it out.

question: Which type of cervical traction involves putting metal pins directly into the skull bone?

options.A: Manual traction
options.B: Halter traction
options.C: Skin traction
options.D: Halo traction

explanation: Great job! Skeletal traction (like a halo device) uses metal pins right in the bone so it can handle much stronger pulling forces.

question: What is the very first step in a standard progressive discipline process?

options.A: Informal verbal warning
options.B: Immediate termination
options.C: Formal written warning
options.D: Temporary suspension

explanation: Progressive discipline starts gently with a private, verbal conversation to address minor issues early. [learn more](GST321_U1_T22#GST321_U1_T22_h5)

question: What do we call using a traditional or home healing practice right alongside standard hospital treatment?

options.A: Alternative medicine
options.B: Biomedical intervention
options.C: Complementary therapy
options.D: Allopathic treatment

explanation: Great job! Complementary therapy means adding practices alongside regular hospital medicine, whereas alternative medicine is used to replace it completely.

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of acute salpingitis?

options.A: Swelling of the lower extremities
options.B: Sharp pain in the upper right shoulder
options.C: Painless enlargement of the abdomen
options.D: Bilateral lower abdominal pain

explanation: Inflammation of the tubes usually causes lower belly and pelvic pain on both sides.

question: Why is working closely with local and religious leaders so vital for successful immunization drives?

options.A: Village leaders are trained to administer routine injections during staff shortages
options.B: Community members fund the importation of foreign vaccine supplies
options.C: Trusted local voices help address fears and clear up cultural misconceptions about vaccines
options.D: Local leaders inspect refrigerator temperatures every morning before clinic opens

explanation: People trust their community leaders. When elders and local leaders support immunization, families feel safe and eager to bring their children forward!

question: If a patient casually mentions they drink a lot of alcohol when you ask about social habits, what should be your first nursing reaction?

options.A: Tell the patient they must stop drinking today
options.B: Acknowledge the disclosure calmly without showing judgment
options.C: Immediately document that the patient has an addiction
options.D: Scold the patient for damaging their liver health

explanation: Spot on! Keeping a cool, non-judgmental attitude makes the patient feel safe enough to keep telling you the truth.

question: Which pathway serves as the main route for conscious, precise voluntary movements?

options.A: Posterior column pathway
options.B: Spinothalamic tract
options.C: Corticospinal tract
options.D: Autonomic reflex arc

explanation: When you decide to write notes or pick up a pen, the corticospinal tract is the master pathway carrying those commands straight from your brain to your muscles.

question: Which of the following conditions is characterized by high lung pressure and the failure of fetal shunts to close properly after birth?

options.A: Congenital liver failure from the ductus venosus
options.B: Neonatal systemic hypotension
options.C: Placental abruption syndrome
options.D: Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn

explanation: PPHN occurs when high pulmonary resistance persists, keeping fetal shunts open and starving the body of oxygen. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h7)

question: What is the main focus of long-term care compared to acute care?

options.A: Performing emergency procedures and trauma resuscitation
options.B: Providing short-term surgical recovery and rapid discharge
options.C: Maintaining quality of life and managing chronic conditions
options.D: Curing acute infections and stabilizing vital signs

explanation: You've got this! While acute care focuses on sudden illnesses, long-term care is all about steady, ongoing support and helping people live well with long-standing health challenges.

question: What is the main concern of 'statistical conclusion validity'?

options.A: Whether the hospital management approved the budget
options.B: Whether the results can be used in other countries
options.C: Whether participants signed their consent forms
options.D: Whether the right math and statistical tests were used to find a true link

explanation: This type of validity makes sure the researchers didn't use the wrong math formulas, so we can trust that their numbers actually mean something.

question: Why is proper cold chain management especially challenging in rural Nigerian healthcare settings?

options.A: Unreliable electricity supply and high ambient temperatures
options.B: Vaccines manufactured locally do not require refrigeration
options.C: An overabundance of modern refrigerated transport trucks
options.D: Lack of community interest in preventive health services

explanation: Erratic power grids and hot weather make keeping vaccines cold a constant logistical hurdle for rural healthcare workers. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h7)

question: Why is the alkaline nature of the fluid from the bulbourethral glands important?

options.A: It stimulates the testes to release more testosterone
options.B: It creates a thick clot to block the vaginal opening
options.C: It freezes sperm to preserve them until intercourse
options.D: It neutralizes leftover acid from urine in the urethra

explanation: Urine leaves acid traces in the urethra that can harm sperm, so the alkaline mucus neutralizes them first. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T3#GNS121_U4_T3_h4)

question: What is one of the best perks of using an electronic blood pressure machine over a manual one?

options.A: They are completely unaffected if the patient moves
options.B: They take very little training to use correctly
options.C: They give exact readings even during serious heart rhythm problems
options.D: They never need new batteries or servicing

explanation: Digital monitors do the heavy lifting for you! You don't need expert stethoscope listening skills to get a quick reading.

question: How often should essential emergency equipment like crash carts be checked on a hospital ward?

options.A: Every shift
options.B: Once a month
options.C: Only after a patient codes
options.D: Once a year

explanation: Routine shift checks ensure that emergency items are present, functional, and ready for immediate use. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h6)

question: What behavior might you notice in a patient who has reached acceptance?

options.A: Conserving energy and withdrawing into quiet reflection
options.B: Arguing with family over small things
options.C: Demanding aggressive new experimental treatments
options.D: Denying that they have any symptoms at all

explanation: As energy fades, patients in acceptance often quiet down, letting go of worldly fuss to rest in peace.

question: Why is it smart for you, as a student nurse, to understand local social patterns before launching a health program?

options.A: To calculate the exact cost of medical supplies needed for outreach
options.B: To diagnose individual patients with chronic infectious diseases
options.C: To legally register the clinic with the federal ministry of health
options.D: To ensure the health intervention fits the local way of life and gains acceptance

explanation: When you respect and understand how people live, they will welcome you and your health programs with open arms. Working with the culture always beats working against it!

question: What security practice involves giving staff access only to the patient files needed for their specific job duties?

options.A: Role-based access control
options.B: Universal computer sharing
options.C: Open public network browsing
options.D: Manual paper chart locking

explanation: Role-based access limits what parts of an EHR a user can see based on their specific job role, protecting patient privacy. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h7)

question: Why is adaptability so important for nurses working in rural clinics?

options.A: They follow rigid routines that never change
options.B: They often face limited resources and must adjust quickly
options.C: They deal exclusively with surgical trauma cases daily
options.D: They do not need to interact with other health workers

explanation: Correct! Rural clinics often lack heavy equipment and specialized staff, so nurses have to be resourceful and flexible to help their patients.

question: Why does the spinal cord have a thicker area called the cervical enlargement?

options.A: To protect the delicate blood vessels entering the skull
options.B: To manage sensory and motor input for the upper limbs
options.C: To anchor the spinal cord firmly to the thoracic cage
options.D: To produce extra cerebrospinal fluid for the brain

explanation: Think of it this way: your arms need a lot of wiring! The spinal cord bulges out in the neck and lower back regions because it has to handle all the heavy nerve traffic going to and from your limbs.
